content.text: : DM, HTN, family hx, ≥60yo, AA, Hispanic, Asian/Pacific Islander, American Indian, NSAIDs, AKI hx
Cardiovascular disease is the leading cause of morbidity/mortality in CKD
: end stage of CKD, defined as severely ↓ kidney function
: chronic kidney failure treated w/ either dialysis or transplantation
(diabetes, autoimmune disease, systemic infections, drugs, neoplasia)
•Chronic allograft nephropathy (non-specific findings of tubular atrophy, interstitial fibrosis, vascular & glomerular sclerosis)
•Granular casts & renal tubular epithelial cells in many parenchymal diseases (non-specific)
: polycystic kidneys, hydronephrosis, cortical scarring, renal masses, enlarged kidneys d/t infiltrative diseases, RAD, small/echogenic kidneys
: NSAIDs, COX-2 inhibitors, antimicrobials, chemo agents, antiretroviral drugs, PPIs, lithium
malaise, weakness, insomnia, inability to concentrate, N/V
, almost always indicates ± some component of AKI
(ie, urinelike breath odor d/t urea + saliva forming ammonia), often assoc w/
progress cog impairment leading to seizures & coma if untx
•Abnorm WBC/immune system functions (more freq & severe infections)
: hyperphosphatemia + hypocalcemia + ↓vitD (calcidiol & calcitriol) lead to 2/2 hyperparathyroidism (ie, ↑ bone turnover)
*all characterized by bone pain & easy fractures
: CBC, CMP, urine dipstick & microscopy, ACR & PCR on random urine sample
= the main protein lost thru urine in CKD
: most useful imaging study, initial TOC
BL sm (<10cm), echogenic kidneys suggest chronic scarring of advanced CKD
•Norm/enlrg kidneys can be seen w/ PKD, diabetic nephropathy, HIV-associated nephropathy, plasma cell myeloma, amyloidosis, obstructive uropathy
: useful if renovascular ischemic dz sus
•identify pts that will require kidney replace therapy
